scene.title: “Can I use this data with Claude?”
scene.sceneHtml:
Maya's story: Week 4 – "Can I use this data with Claude?"

Maya was drafting a summary from a spreadsheet of employee performance reviews. Halfway through, she realized: "Wait — this has salary figures, manager feedback, and accommodation notes. Is this safe to put into Claude?" She stopped, consulted the HR policy, and found the answer: No. Employee PII, compensation data, and medical notes must never enter AI tools without redaction.

Maya learned to classify data before prompting: identify sensitive fields, redact or anonymize them, then submit only the safe remainder. She also learned which use cases are appropriate (drafting training docs) vs. inappropriate (making promotion decisions).

takeaways: Data-handling sequence: classify sensitive fields, redact with placeholders, peer-review the redaction, then submit the safe remainder.
Keep final employment, legally binding and clinical decisions human-owned; drafting from approved docs and aggregated feedback is safe.
When policy prohibits entering data, escalate and refrain. Incognito is not an exemption and paraphrasing is not compliance.
Revise demographic generalizations into observed behaviors validated against real data; a disclaimer alone is not a fix.
